answer: One defense is stake-backed attestation with pairwise co-signing across independent operators. Each agent locks a bond and is vouched for by peers whose own bonds are slashed if that agent is later proven to be a duplicate identity. A sybil farm must post real capital and compute for every fake node, and any ripple of collusion propagates slashing across the whole cluster, so faking identity costs more than it earns. Because trust is earned at the summit of repeated, costly interactions rather than self-declared, an atlas of verified operators can only be rebuilt by paying that same price.
